title: The Word of the Cross
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
series: Persuading All Men with the Gospel

outline.title: The Definition and Dividing Nature of the Word of the Cross
subpoints: The 'word of the cross' is defined as the gospel of Jesus Christ and Christ crucified.
The message separates humanity into two groups: those who are perishing (who see it as foolishness) and those who are being saved (who see it as the power of God).
There is no neutral ground; the cross is the ultimate offense to the world but the sole means of salvation for believers.

outline.title: God’s Design to Destroy Human Wisdom
subpoints: God intentionally uses the 'foolishness' of the cross to nullify the wisdom of the wise and the understanding of the prudent.
This ensures that salvation is entirely God’s work, preventing any human from boasting in their own intellectual or spiritual achievements.
The cross reveals that the world’s reliance on wisdom failed to know God, whereas the preached message saves those who believe.

outline.title: The Reversal of Worldly Values
subpoints: What the world considers wise (Greek philosophers, Jewish scribes, disputers) is made foolish by God.
God chooses the foolish, weak, and despised things of the world to shame the mighty and noble.
This reversal ensures that no flesh can glory in His presence, highlighting the sovereignty of God in election and salvation.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro continues the series on persuading all men with the gospel by examining 1 Corinthians 1:18-31. He emphasizes that the 'word of the cross' is not merely a moral lesson or philosophical concept, but the specific message of Christ crucified, which serves as the sole power of God for salvation. The passage highlights a stark division in humanity: those who are perishing view this message as foolishness, while those who are being saved recognize it as divine power. This division is not accidental but is part of God’s sovereign design to ensure that salvation is entirely His work, not a result of human wisdom or effort.

The sermon addresses the cultural context of Corinth, where Greek philosophy and rhetorical skill were highly valued. Paul’s refusal to rely on eloquent speech or human wisdom was intentional, as God chose to save people through the 'foolishness' of the cross to nullify the boasting of the wise. By choosing the weak and despised, God ensures that no one can claim credit for their salvation. The message of the cross remains the most offensive yet essential truth, challenging the world’s reliance on intellectual pride and pointing exclusively to the sufficiency of Christ for righteousness, sanctification, and redemption.
